newsitem.title: INDIA: India oil price hike could pull down rupee - dealers.
newsitem.headline: India oil price hike could pull down rupee - dealers.

text.p: A proposed increase in petroleum product prices in India could provide an opportunity to the government to correct an overvalued rupee, bank dealers said on Friday.
The United Front coalition's steering committee meets on June 15 to take a decision on hiking petroleum product prices.
Dealers said oil companies have not been paid their dues for a long time from the oil pool account that manages the subsidies, they said.
A price increase would generate rupee revenues to pay the oil firms who could then be asked to buy their dollar requirements from the spot market, pushing up dollar demand.
The Indian Oil Corporation in recent months has been depending on external commercial borrowings for its dollar requirements to fund imports.
"They did something similar in 1995 when the government decided to tap the market for debt repayments," a dealer said.
The rupee has been rising against the dollar in recent months because of weak dollar demand and abundant supplies.
Dealers said the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) appeared to be intervening reluctantly to arrest the rupee's rise in recent weeks.
The RBI has earlier said its intervention was constrained by its impact on domestic liquidity.
"We are in a situation where lot of non-trade related funds are flowing into India," said an economist at a research firm.
"If RBI buys dollars aggressively, it will feed inflation."
Gross inward remittances amounted to $10.0 billion in 1996/97 against $7.5 billion a year ago, he said.
Most of the India Development Bonds worth about $2.5 billion which were repaid in 1996/97 did not leave the country as much of it was retained in non-resident accounts.

Indian exporters have recently been clamouring for a depreciation of the rupee, saying the overvalued rupee was hurting competitiveness especially in the light of depreciation of currencies of neighbouring countries.
